label: encryption key rotation
type: replacing an encryption key with a new one on a schedule. Asymmetric by default: Couchbase Server rotates DEKs automatically but does NOT rotate the encryption-at-rest keys themselves unless that is explicitly enabled - and keys held in an external KMS cannot be rotated by Couchbase Server at all.
evidence: By default, Couchbase Server automatically rotates DEKs but not the encryption keys it uses to encrypt them.
To rotate an encryption-at-rest key managed by an external KMS, you must use the KMS's tools.
Rotation of an externally managed encryption key is handled by the KMS that manage it.
note: Filed with encryption:drop-deks-rest-action because the documentation goes out of its way to distinguish them - 'Dropping DEKs is not the same as rotating DEKs' - which is the `shouldNotBeConfusedWith` predicate earning its keep. The KMS asymmetry is the operationally important part: enabling an external KMS silently moves a rotation responsibility outside Couchbase Server.
